overview.summary: Ireland is an English-speaking EU country with a strong technology and pharmaceutical sector. Graduates can stay for 12 or 24 months to look for work, depending on their qualification level.
overview.educationSystem: Universities, technological universities and colleges award qualifications on the National Framework of Qualifications (NFQ). Honours bachelor’s degrees are Level 8; master’s degrees are Level 9. Most taught master’s programmes take one year.

courses.description: Typical length; the exact duration depends on the institution and programme.

financialEvidence.requirement: You must have immediate access to at least €10,000 for each year of study (courses over eight months), in addition to course fees. Visa-required applicants are checked at the visa stage.

postStudyRoutes.name: Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G)

duration.value: 12 months for Level 8; up to 24 months for Level 9 or higher
duration.label: official

postStudyRoutes.conditions: Hold current Stamp 2, apply within six months of your results, and stay within the overall time limits for students. You can work full-time but cannot be self-employed.

postStudyRoutes.name: Critical Skills or General Employment Permit
postStudyRoutes.conditions: Requires an eligible job offer and salary.

postStudyRoutes.name: Long-term residence
postStudyRoutes.conditions: Separate rules; study time does not lead to residence automatically.

lifestyle.text: Housing is the biggest challenge. Book student residence early and be wary of rental scams.
Buses, DART and Luas in Dublin. The student Leap card reduces fares.
Private medical insurance is required; GP visits usually involve a fee.
Generally safe. Keep your IRP card and registration up to date.
